findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, delete_inbox, search · Private data: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, get_event, extract_field, delete_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, search · Destructive: delete_inbox.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, delete_inbox, search · Private data: create_inbox, wait_for_event, list_events, get_event, extract_field, delete_inbox · Public sink: create_inbox, search · Destructive: delete_inbox

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_inbox" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
